_doc: SINGLE coverage ledger for conformance fixtures that the plain differential
oracle (packages/runar-testing/src/oracle/differential-execution.ts) does NOT
execute. It answers one question per fixture: why is this fixture not covered
by the plain oracle, and what covers it INSTEAD?
Consolidated from the two files this replaces — `crypto-exempt.json` (array
key `exempt`) and `harness-inapplicable.json` (array key `inapplicable`) —
which were the same mechanism read by the same tests, differing only in that
the second carried a `cause` discriminator. Every entry now carries that
discriminator, so the two axes are still distinguishable without two files.
Schema — one object per fixture under `entries`:
fixture   — directory name under conformance/tests/ (must exist; typos are
caught by completeness.test.ts, duplicates by
coverage-claims.test.ts)
cause     — WHY the plain oracle cannot run it (vocabulary below; enforced
by coverage-claims.test.ts)
reason    — free-text, FOR HUMANS ONLY. Never machine-checked and never
treated as evidence. Several of these strings record a real bug
and its fix; do not paraphrase them away.
coveredBy — the MACHINE-CHECKED claim of what actually covers the fixture.
coverage-claims.test.ts proves each claim by grepping the
artifact it names.
`cause` vocabulary (the closed set enforced in coverage-claims.test.ts):
crypto-witness-infeasible — the spend needs a REAL cryptographic witness
(ECDSA/Schnorr checkSig, secp256k1 / NIST-P EC, SHA-256 / BLAKE3 /
Merkle hash-preimage, Rabin, or a post-quantum SLH-DSA / WOTS+
signature) that the in-process oracle cannot synthesise from bare args.
These are the entries formerly in `crypto-exempt.json`. Post-mortem
remediation #1 gave the oracle REAL secp256k1: every stateless/stateful
ECDSA-checkSig / checkMultiSig fixture that could be given a real
signature was MOVED to conformance/witnesses/real-crypto/ (executed for
real on @bsv/sdk Spend) and removed from the ledger. What remains under
this cause is genuinely out of reach for the current TS real-crypto
harness. NOTE: this cause also records PROVENANCE — it marks every entry
that came from `crypto-exempt.json`, so the pre-merge partition stays
recoverable. A few of them (all-readonly-cleanstack, covenant-vault) are
really stateful-harness gaps, and merkle-proof / state-covenant are
really go-only, as their own `reason` and `coveredBy` say; they were
filed in the crypto ledger historically and were NOT reclassified during
the merge. Reclassify deliberately, not as a side effect.
stateful-harness-gap — non-crypto: the SDK deploy->call->Spend continuation
path cannot reconstruct the exact tx shape a StatefulSmartContract
method demands. Remediation #1 added that real path (runar-testing
runStatefulSpend) and MOVED every stateful fixture whose continuation
could be driven and re-validated on @bsv/sdk Spend with a real
checkPreimage binding out of the ledger; what remains still cannot be
composed by it.
go-only — a compilers:["go"] proof-system fixture: no TypeScript Stack-IR
codegen exists, so compile() cannot emit deployed bytes for the TS-based
harness to run.
interpreter-unsupported — the ANF interpreter (source-semantics engine) does
not model the intrinsic the fixture uses, so the differential /
real-crypto oracles cannot execute it at all.
CONTRACTS THIS FILE IS HELD TO (both enforced in code, not just documented):
1. Membership in this ledger is NOT itself coverage. The machine-checked
truth of an entry's claim lives in `coveredBy`, verified by
coverage-claims.test.ts against the artifact it names — the fix for a
past bug where entries claimed a script_execution_test.go execution path
that did not reference the fixture at all.
2. `coveredBy.kind === "UNCOVERED"` is an HONEST HOLE, NOT COVERAGE.
completeness.test.ts deliberately does not count such an entry as
covered, so the top-level completeness gate fails on it BY DESIGN and the
hole cannot hide behind list membership (audit findings #P0-1, #11, #14,
#24). UNCOVERED additionally requires a non-empty `issue` field.
The `coveredBy.kind` vocabulary is documented in conformance/witnesses/README.md
and enforced in conformance/witnesses/coverage-claims.test.ts. Other ledgers in
the repo (golden-provenance-allowlist.json, fold-on-allowlist.json,
sdk-output/coverage-allowlist.json, source-map/anchor-known-issues.json) are
DIFFERENT axes and deliberately stay separate — see the README section
"Why the other ledgers stay separate".

entries.reason: sendToScript(): a TWO-output method — addRawOutput(1000, scriptBytes) plus the addOutput(0, count) state continuation. The SDK deploy->call->Spend path (real-crypto/ style) funds a single continuation output; it does not fund/emit the separate 1000-sat raw output, so a real Spend rejects (checkPreimage output binding fails). RESOLVED (audit P0 follow-up): the SDK deploy->call path still can't compose this, but conformance/script_execution_test.go now hand-builds the exact 3-output tx (raw output, state continuation, change) via executeScriptWithTx and gets a genuine tx-context accept/reject differential against the compiled Bitcoin Script bytes — TestRawOutput_ScriptExecution_Accept (raw output present) and TestRawOutput_ScriptExecution_Reject_RawOutputAbsent (raw output omitted from the real tx while the unlocking script still claims it) — superseding the ANF-interpreter-only anf-cross-tier-parity coverage below as the primary claim.

zero-mutable-field StatefulSmartContract (issue #44): RunarContract.prepareCall derives isStateful from stateFields.length>0, which is false here, so it exposes the auto-injected SigHashPreimage as a REQUIRED user arg and the standard call([null]) continuation path does not apply — the tx-context preimage cannot be supplied via the SDK call() harness. FOLLOW-UP: drive it via a hand-built preimage in the TS harness.

coveredBy.note: real deploy + terminal claim() spend on a live regtest node (accept-only; gated behind `cargo test --features regtest`); proves the parentClass sighash-trim fix, not a full accept/reject differential.

entries.reason: UnsafeSmartContract asm({body:'51'}) raw-script intrinsic is not implemented by the ANF interpreter (source-semantics engine reports 'Unknown function: asm'), so the differential / real-crypto oracles cannot execute it. Instead the compiled OP_1 is executed directly on the go-sdk Bitcoin Script engine (anyone-can-spend, empty unlocking → clean TRUE); deliberately no reject case, since universal acceptance is the contract's semantics.

Nearest existing execution, and why it is not this: compilers/go/codegen/script_correctness_test.go TestBBExt4Inv_Script / _WrongResult really does run script through the go-sdk interpreter against those vectors, but it assembles gatherOps(EmitBBExt4Inv0..3) inline at the Stack-IR level — Inv only, not Mul, and not this fixture's composed bytes. integration/go/fri_colinearity_vectors_test.go TestFRI_Vectors_Accept spends real ext4-Mul on regtest, but of an inline FRIColinearityCheck contract, not this fixture. Neither is a byte-matched spend of babybear-ext4, so neither may be cited here.

entries.reason: Stateless codegen-coverage fixture for split / int2str / reverseBytes / ripemd160 / the Sha256Hash alias. Neither witness form can drive it: a differential witness needs crypto to mock and this contract calls none beyond a bare OP_SHA256 / OP_RIPEMD160, and a real-crypto witness drives deploy->call against a state continuation this stateless contract does not have. It is NOT uncovered. conformance/byte_builtins_execution_test.go compiles the fixture with a baked SHA-256 digest and a baked RIPEMD-160 digest and SPENDS the resulting locking script on the go-sdk consensus interpreter, at each builtin's boundaries -- split at 0, at len, on the empty string and out of range; int2str at zero, negative, zero width and a width too small for the value; reverseBytes at 0, 1, odd and 520 bytes, the maximum BSV element; and, for each of the two hashes, the preimage accepted while the DIGEST ITSELF is refused. Every group carries negative rows, so a script that ignored its arguments could not pass. ripemd160 was the last builtin to reach this fixture: the Go surface's only spelling for it, runar.Ripemd160, is both a Runar type name and a Runar builtin name, and two of the seven tiers resolved the call as a type cast -- dropping OP_RIPEMD160 and making the baked digest the spending key -- so until that was fixed no fixture could call it. See conformance/go_surface_hash_spelling_execution_test.go.

entries.reason: payBond() is a TERMINAL StatefulSmartContract method that asserts output 0 is a bond P2PKH via requireOutputP2PKH(0, ...) with no state mutation, so there is no state continuation and output 0 is free. The SDK deploy->call->Spend path does not compose an external bond output, so there is no go-script-exec accept/reject differential; covered instead by the ANF interpreter (1 accept + 2 reject: correct witness, wrong PKH bytes, wrong hashOutputs) across all 7 tiers. NOTE: the earlier variant that mixed requireOutputP2PKH(0) with a state mutation (the implicit single-output continuation ALSO claiming output 0, making it permanently unspendable) is now a COMPILE-TIME ERROR — see the guard in packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/03-typecheck.ts and TestIntentOutputP2PKH_GuardRejectsMutatingVariant in conformance/script_execution_test.go.

coveredBy.note: 1 accept + 2 reject (wrong PKH bytes, wrong hashOutputs) executed via the ANF interpreter with witness-injected serialised outputs (TestContract.setSerialisedOutputs / setMockPreimageBytes), mirrored per-tier in the runar-{go,rs,py,zig,rb,java} intent interpreter tests. Not a full Bitcoin Script byte execution.

entries.reason: bind(): extractPrevOutputScript(0, expectedHash) asserts hash256(witness) === expectedHash, a constructor-baked readonly field — the witness-bridge pattern documented in docs/cross-covenant-pattern.md (it does NOT itself introspect input 0's real prevout script; only the current input's own BIP-143 preimage fields are available to Bitcoin Script). RESOLVED (audit P0 follow-up): the earlier 'circular' framing assumed input 0 must be the contract's own (self-referential, hence impossible) UTXO; conformance/script_execution_test.go instead builds a real TWO-input transaction where input 0 carries an independent companion prevout (whose real locking script is the witness) and input 1 carries the contract's own UTXO being spent — TestIntentPrevOutputScript_ScriptExecution_Accept (witness bytes hash to expectedHash, genuinely equal to input 0's real prevout script) and TestIntentPrevOutputScript_ScriptExecution_Reject_WrongWitness (tampered witness bytes) — a real tx-context accept/reject differential against the compiled Bitcoin Script bytes.

entries.reason: Stateless codegen-coverage fixture for p256Negate / p256EncodeCompressed -- same shape as byte-builtins: no mockable crypto for a differential witness, no state continuation for a real-crypto one. conformance/p256_p384_encode_negate_execution_test.go spends its compiled script on the go-sdk consensus interpreter against P-256 arithmetic reimplemented from the NIST parameters in math/big: negate on G and a derived point, the involution negate(negate(P)) == P, y == 0 reducing to 0 rather than to p, non-canonical x == p and y == p refused, over- and under-length blobs refused, compression in BOTH parities with the flipped prefix refused, and the CL-BUG-095 appended-byte attack refused.

coveredBy.note: real deploy + SPEND on a live regtest node: TestSLHDSA_ValidSpend (accept — real ECDSA signature over the spending input, then a real SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s signature over those bytes via runar.SLHSign, confirmed with AssertTxAccepted) plus TestSLHDSA_TamperedSig_Rejected and TestSLHDSA_WrongECDSASig_Rejected (AssertTxRejected). getSLHDSAArtifact compiles examples/ts/sphincs-wallet/SPHINCSWallet.runar.ts — the exact .runar.ts source this fixture resolves to — verified 2026-08-06 to be BYTE-IDENTICAL to this fixture's expected-script.hex (188,609 bytes, in BOTH fold modes), so the node executed this fixture's own bytes with only the two constructorSlots substituted.
